cleanIntro: Nothing comes off a Model 350 for cleaning except the compensator, if yours has one. What this revolver adds to the X-Frame routine is the moon clip: .350 Legend is rimless, so the clips are part of the gun's cycle and get inspected and cleaned like any other component.

steps.title: Confirm you are holding an X-Frame, not a J, K, L, N or Governor
steps.action: Check that the revolver in front of you is an X-Frame chambered for 350 Legend before you use a single step here. This book is for the X-Frame revolvers only; Smith & Wesson prints separate manuals for its J, K, L and N-Frame revolvers, for the Governor, and again for the M&P BODYGUARD 38.
steps.prose: The Model 350 is the seven-shot .350 Legend member of the X-Frame family, and its moon-clip handling is unlike anything in the J/K/L/N book. The model name and number are stamped inside the yoke and only readable with the cylinder swung out, so this check costs the same motion as the unload that follows.
steps.quote: There are separate manuals for S&W® (J, K, L, N-Frame, and Governor) revolvers and the M&P® BODYGUARD®38 revolver - these manuals are available free upon request or via download from our web site.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Cover page, p.1

steps.title: Thumbpiece forward, cylinder out to the left
steps.action: Keep your finger off the trigger and outside the trigger guard, press the thumbpiece fully forward and hold it, then push the cylinder out to the left. Look into all seven charge holes and then down the bore from the muzzle.
steps.prose: Hold the thumbpiece forward through the whole swing or the cylinder stop drags in its notch. Seven holes is two more than the rest of the X-Frame family, so the count you are used to from a five-shot is wrong here — check each hole, and check whether a moon clip is still sitting in the cylinder with rounds on it.
steps.quote: Press the thumbpiece fully forward and hold it, then push the cylinder to the left (FIGURE 5).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Inspecting Your Revolver, p.13

steps.title: Muzzle up, extractor rod through, clip and all
steps.action: With the cylinder held out and the muzzle tipped upward in a safe direction, press the extractor rod toward the cylinder and take out every cartridge or empty case. Where a moon clip was used the cases come out still held on the clip and stay there until you physically pull them free.
steps.prose: This is the part that surprises people coming off a rimmed-cartridge revolver: the ejection stroke lifts the whole clip as one piece rather than dropping loose brass, so 'nothing fell out' is not evidence the cylinder is empty. If the revolver was loaded without clips instead, the ejector has almost no rim to push on and the rounds have to be picked or pushed out individually with a tool such as a wooden dowel.
steps.quote: The cartridges or empty casings will stay in the moon clip until they are physically pulled free from the clip.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Use of Moon Clips in Model 350, p.21

steps.title: Nothing marked +P+ goes in this revolver
steps.action: Check what you have been shooting: ammunition marked +P+ must not be used in this firearm. That covers the rifle-intended .350 Legend loads on the shelf as much as anything else — a headstamp marking is not a clearance.
steps.prose: Smith & Wesson's stated reason is that +P+ names no defined pressure limit at all; it is a loader's own marking, so two boxes wearing it can be a long way apart in what they actually generate. Standard +P is permitted but the manual warns it affects wear characteristics and brings service forward, which in a revolver you notice as endshake and a widening barrel/cylinder gap.
steps.caution: "Plus-P-Plus" (+P+) ammunition must NOT be used in Smith & Wesson firearms.
steps.quote: “Plus-P-Plus” (+P+) ammunition must NOT be used in Smith & Wesson® firearms. This marking on the ammunition designates that it exceeds established industry standards, but the designation does not represent defined pressure limits and therefore such ammunition may vary significantly as to the pressures generated and could be DANGEROUS.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Ammunition, +P+ paragraph, p.11

steps.title: Read the barrel marking, and fire only 350 Legend
steps.action: Read the cartridge designation rolled on your barrel and fire only what it names. The manual's own moon-clip section for the Model 350 states in capitals that cartridges other than those specified on the barrel marking may fit into the chambers but must not be used in this firearm, and that injury or death to the shooter or bystanders and damage to property may result.
steps.prose: This warning is printed under the Model 350 heading specifically, and it earns its place here: .350 Legend is a straight-walled rimless case of a diameter shared with other cartridges, so something wrong will seat in a charge hole without protest. The alternate-ammunition table on page 11 lists substitutes for the 500 and the 460 and lists none for the 350 — there is no second cartridge for this revolver.
steps.quote: CARTRIDGES OTHER THAN THOSE SPECIFIED ON THE BARREL MARKING MAY FIT INTO THE CHAMBERS BUT MUST NOT BE USED IN THIS FIREARM. INJURY AND/OR DEATH TO THE SHOOTER OR BYSTANDERS AND DAMAGE TO PROPERTY MAY RESULT.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Ammunition, p.9 (barrel-marking warning at p.20)
steps.warn: Cartridges other than those specified on the barrel marking may fit into the chambers but must not be used in this firearm.

steps.title: Inspect the moon clips as you strip them
steps.action: Pull each case straight out of the clip in the direction of the clip opening, prying the first one loose with a dull tool if the tension is high, then look the clip over. A broken, bent or cracked clip is discarded and replaced, not straightened.
steps.prose: The clip is a headspacing part on this revolver, not an accessory: a bent clip holds a rimless case out of position and gives light strikes, hard extraction or a cylinder that will not close. Getting the first case out relieves the tension on the rest, which is why they fight you until one lets go.
steps.quote: Inspect the moon clip after each use. If broken, bent or cracked, discard and replace the moon clip.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Use of Moon Clips in Model 350, p.21

steps.title: Inspect the forcing cone while the cylinder is open
steps.action: With the cylinder still swung out, look into the rear of the barrel at the forcing cone and compare it with the good and eroded examples the manual prints. Smith & Wesson asks for this before use, not only at cleaning time.
steps.prose: Erosion at the forcing cone is the failure that opens up a barrel, and it is where the gas escaping the cylinder gap does its work. A smooth even funnel is what you want; flame cutting and a ragged crescent at the top mean the barrel goes back to the factory for replacement rather than through another cleaning cycle.
steps.quote: Before using a Smith & Wesson® revolver, you should open the cylinder and inspect the barrel forcing cone to ensure that it is in good working condition.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Inspecting Forcing Cone of Smith & Wesson X-Frame Revolvers, p.14

steps.title: If yours wears the removable compensator, take it off
steps.action: Insert a 2.5mm hex wrench into the screw under the compensator, below the muzzle opening, and turn it CLOCKWISE until the lock screw stops — roughly two to three turns. Rotate the compensator a quarter turn either way with your fingers and pull it forward off the barrel.
steps.prose: This is the only component the manual removes from an X-Frame, and only on guns fitted with it. The lock screw releases clockwise, which is backwards from the reflex that clockwise tightens; if the compensator will not rotate by hand, the cross holes in its body take the wrench for leverage.
steps.quote: Remove the compensator from the barrel for cleaning or for a compensator change (FIGURE 34).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Removable Compensator, Removal Instructions, p.29

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You have an open, empty seven-shot cylinder, your moon clips stripped and inspected, and — if the gun was so fitted — a compensator off the barrel. That is the whole of what Smith & Wesson publishes for the Model 350; cylinder, yoke, hammer and lockwork all stay in the frame. Deep Clean carries the record of why for this listing.
steps.prose: The limit is stated in the manual rather than implied: it forbids going past the procedure it prints, and it prints no disassembly at all.
steps.quote: NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR FIREARM BEYOND THE FIELD STRIPPING/DISASSEMBLY PROCEDURE DETAILED IN THIS MANUAL, OR PERFORM ANY MAINTENANCE, ADJUSTMENT, OR SERVICE NOT SPECIFIED.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR S&W® X-FRAME REVOLVERS — REV:S&W_X-FRAME_REVOLVERS_033025 — Cleaning and Maintenance, p.31

deepAbsentReason: The X-Frame manual documents opening and unloading the cylinder, moon-clip loading, unloading and inspection, forcing-cone inspection, removal and refitting of the removable compensator, cleaning, lubrication and storage — and publishes no disassembly of the revolver whatsoever. Its table of contents carries no field-stripping or disassembly section at all, and p.31 forbids going beyond what it prints.

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHARGE HOLES
tasks: Remove excessive firing residue from the bore and all seven charge holes with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent
Finish each with a dry cotton patch to carry out residue and solvent
Clean the cylinder face and the underside of the extractor star
Clean the moon clip recesses cut into the rear of the cylinder — a fouled recess holds the clip proud and the cylinder will not close

cleaning.name: MOON CLIPS
tasks: Strip every clip after use and clean it
Inspect each clip for breaks, bends and cracks; discard and replace rather than straightening
Push cartridges straight in when reloading a clip, to avoid bending it
Keep spare clips — Smith & Wesson sells them by part number through dealers and Customer Service

cleaning.name: COMPENSATOR (IF FITTED)
tasks: With the compensator off, clean its bore channel and ports of carbon and lead
Clean the muzzle end of the barrel it seats on, and the lock screw and notch
Fit the compensator pattern that matches what you shoot — one is specified for jacketed bullets, the other for lead

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR, LUBRICATION AND STORAGE
tasks: Clean the exterior with a non-abrasive cloth and remove all solution, oil and fingerprints — finger moisture left on steel starts a corrosion process
Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning; never use ammoniated or strong alkaline solvents
After cleaning, lightly coat the metal parts inside and out with a high quality gun oil
For extended storage oil the bore, charge holes and internal mechanism, coat the external mechanism and barrel with an anti-rust oil, and do not store the revolver in leather or heavy cloth
Check for signs of wear every time you clean it; if wear is noted, do not use the revolver

reassembly: If the compensator was removed: insert it into the front of the barrel shroud, rotate it with your fingers until the notch faces down in the 6 o'clock position, then hold it and turn the 2.5mm hex wrench COUNTERCLOCKWISE until the lock screw stops — two to three turns. Do not overtighten.
Close the cylinder into the frame and confirm it locks up.
Load a clean clip only when you are ready to shoot; check that it seats flush and that the cylinder closes without force.
fncheck: With all seven charge holes confirmed empty and the bore clear, close the cylinder and check it latches and that the thumbpiece releases it cleanly. Cycle the action double action and single action pointed in a safe direction and confirm the cylinder indexes and locks at every stop. Then seat an empty moon clip in the cylinder and confirm it drops fully into the recesses and the cylinder still closes without force — a clip that stands proud is either bent or the recesses are fouled.
